record_identity.title: 11 June 2026 — Agent Work Is Not Complete Until It Is Recoverable

report_title: 11 June 2026 — Agent Work Is Not Complete Until It Is Recoverable
case_descriptor: Lessons from quota exhaustion, ephemeral agent work loss, and non-recoverable interruption
summary: Substantive agent work is not durably complete while it exists only inside an ephemeral, inaccessible, session-bound, or quota-dependent environment. A governed runtime should establish recoverable work state proportionate to task cost and interruption risk, reserve capacity for minimum persistence, distinguish processing from durable delivery, and preserve a manual continuation path even when later administration fails.
what_happened: On 11 June 2026, a Codex cloud task performed substantive multi-file repository work but exhausted the user's available allowance before creating a durable branch, commit, patch, or equivalent recovery artefact.

The task remained suspended and later failed, leaving the completed modifications inaccessible and requiring the user to repeat work estimated to consume approximately 15 percent of the available daily Codex allocation.
The linked repair established durable work-state, safe-boundary pause, persistence-budget, checkpoint, delivery-posture, recovery-record, and specific infrastructure-continuity failure controls.
governance_misconception: Substantive processing inside an ephemeral agent environment was treated as meaningful completion even though no user-accessible, recoverable work product existed.

Branch creation, commit, patch export, or equivalent checkpointing was deferred until after the expensive transformation, leaving persistence dependent on residual quota, time, authentication, tool, and infrastructure availability.
Pull-request creation was treated as the first or only useful durability boundary, rather than one downstream administrative step after minimum recoverability has already been secured.
abstracted_learning: For materially consequential agent work, recoverability is part of completion. The runtime should create and maintain a proportionate recovery pathway before interruption risk can erase the work, prioritise minimum persistence when execution capacity becomes constrained, and represent substantive completion separately from durable delivery.
integrated_learning: Long-running, quota-consuming, externally mutating, repository-connected, or file-transforming tasks require recoverable work state proportionate to their cost, mutation depth, duration, and interruption risk.

A durable branch, pushed or committed checkpoint, temporary recoverable workspace, stash, patch, diff, checkpointed artefact, task-state manifest, or resumable reference may satisfy minimum recoverability according to context.

Where quota, timeout, authentication, network, tool, device, session, or infrastructure risk becomes material, preservation of minimum recoverable state should take priority over optional validation, packaging, publication, or pull-request administration.

Task interfaces and records should distinguish processing, checkpointed, paused, resumable, substantively complete but undelivered, durably delivered, failed with recoverable state, and failed without recoverable state.

Failure of a pull request, deployment, publication, or final administrative action is not total work loss where the substantive result remains accessible for review, rollback, transfer, reconstruction, or manual continuation.
Temporary preservation does not imply user approval, adoption, merge authority, deployment authority, or permission to modify a protected branch.
risk_if_not_integrated: Quota, timeout, authentication, session, network, tool, or infrastructure failure may erase materially completed work and force duplicate execution.
Users may incur avoidable cost, quota depletion, delay, supervision burden, and loss of confidence in autonomous coding or operational agents.
Interfaces may misrepresent ephemeral processing as completion, preventing users from understanding that no durable deliverable exists.
The absence of checkpoint and recovery records may make it impossible to reconstruct what was completed, what changed, what remains unverified, and whether safe resumption is possible.
Treating pull-request creation as the first persistence boundary may convert a downstream administrative failure into total work-product loss.
future_application: Cloud coding agents and repository-connected assistants
Browser, research, data-processing, and document-transformation agents
Quota-limited, rate-limited, session-bound, or timeout-prone execution
Mobile, intermittent-network, and device-dependent agent workflows
High-cost or externally mutating tasks requiring pause, transfer, rollback, or manual recovery
generalisation_boundary: This lesson does not guarantee successful task completion, immediate interruption during unsafe atomic operations, pull-request creation, deployment, publication, or indefinite storage of every intermediate state. Recoverability must remain proportionate to task consequence and technical feasibility, and temporary system-generated work remains unapproved until the authorised human or process adopts it.
